## File: README.md

# auth-kit

**Authentication and permissions for the MGPL Diagnostics backend, as an internal API.**
There is no HTTP server here. Your backend (GraphQL resolvers, REST handlers, jobs) calls these functions.

![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/checks-128-14264A) ![deps](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20dependencies-0-E9A23B)

## What it does

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Passwords** | scrypt (N=2¹⁵), salted, self-describing hashes; weaker hashes upgraded on the next login; NIST-style policy (length, common passwords, repeated characters, no email) |
| **Login** | rate-limited per IP (failed attempts only: an office of staff on one connection can all sign in) and per email; timing-safe (an unknown email costs the same as a wrong password); same email in several organisations → `ORG_REQUIRED`; audited |
| **Sessions** | opaque tokens, stored only as SHA-256; idle timeout that slides with use plus an absolute maximum age; list devices, revoke one, log out everywhere |
| **JWT mode** | short-lived HS256 access tokens plus single-use refresh tokens, rotated on every refresh; a refresh token used twice ends its session (theft); secret rotation; logout and revocation still apply at once |
| **Accounts** | disabling a user or changing roles applies on the very next request |
| **Passwords, again** | change (keeps this device, ends the others); reset (single-use, expiring token; ends every session); admin set |
| **Permissions** | `resource:action` with wildcards; roles per branch or organisation-wide; built-in lab roles plus each organisation's own |
| **Stores** | memory (tests, one server) or Redis (`/redis`, shared by all servers) |

## Use

```ts
import { createAuth, SYSTEM_ROLES } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit";
import { redisKeyValueStore, redisRateLimiter, redisSessionStore } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit/redis";

// db-kit's repositories satisfy the user / org / role / audit stores as they are
const auth = createAuth({
  users: db.repos.users,
  orgs: db.repos.orgs,
  roles: db.repos.roles,
  audit: db.repos.audit,
  sessions: redisSessionStore(redis),
  kv: redisKeyValueStore(redis),
  limiter: redisRateLimiter(redis, { limit: 10, windowMs: 15 * 60_000 }),
});

const { token, user } = await auth.login({ email, password, ip, userAgent });

// per request, e.g. in the GraphQL context
const { viewer, can, branchesFor } = await auth.context(bearerToken);
can("invoice:create", branchId);   // true / false
branchesFor("booking:read");        // "all" or ["branch-id", …]
```

When you create an organisation, seed the roles: `seedOrganization(repos, { …, roles: SYSTEM_ROLES })`
(db-kit). To create a user, call `auth.hashNewPassword(password, { email })`, which checks the policy
and then hashes.

## JWT mode (access + refresh tokens)

Pass `jwt` and login returns a short-lived **access token** (an HS256 JWT, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`)
and a long-lived **refresh token** (opaque, single-use). The client trades the refresh token for a new pair
when the access token expires.

```ts
const auth = createAuth({ …, kv: redisKeyValueStore(redis), jwt: { secret: process.env.JWT_SECRET!, issuer: "mgpl-api", accessTtlMs: 15 * 60_000 } });

const { token: accessToken, refreshToken } = await auth.login({ email, password });
const ctx = await auth.context(accessToken);                    // same context as before
const next = await auth.refresh({ refreshToken });              // { accessToken, refreshToken (new), … }
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant A as auth-kit
  participant S as Session store
  participant K as kv (Redis)
  C->>A: login(email, password)
  A->>S: session { id: random }
  A->>K: refresh:hash(R1) → session id
  A-->>C: access JWT (sub, org, sid, exp 15 min) + R1
  C->>A: context(JWT) — every request
  A->>A: verify HS256, exp
  A->>S: session still there? re-read the user
  C->>A: refresh(R1)
  A->>K: take refresh:hash(R1) (single use)
  A->>K: refresh:hash(R2) → sid · refresh-used:hash(R1)
  A-->>C: new JWT + R2
  C->>A: refresh(R1) again (stolen copy)
  A->>S: delete the session → JWT and R2 die
```

- **Revocation stays instant.** The JWT carries the session id, and every request checks that the session
  still exists and re-reads the user (rule 3). The signature alone is enough only for
  `verifyAccessToken(token)`, which workers and other services can use without storage.
- **Refresh tokens rotate.** Each is single-use and stored only as a hash. A spent token presented again
  within `reuseGraceMs` (default 15 s, two tabs refreshing at once) is just refused; later, it ends the
  session.
- **Lifetimes.** Access: `accessTtlMs` (default 15 min). Refresh: the session's idle window, slid by each
  refresh, and never past the absolute maximum age.
- **Secrets.** At least 32 characters. Pass `secret: [newSecret, oldSecret]` to rotate: the first signs and
  all verify.
- `logout` accepts the access token (even expired), the refresh token, or an opaque session token.

### Device binding

Clients can send security signals with `login` and `refresh` (`device: DeviceSignals`). They are cleaned
(`cleanDeviceSignals`: ids 8–128 safe characters, at most 20 short `info` values) and stored on the session.

| Signal | What it is | On refresh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deviceId` | random id the client keeps per browser profile or app install | must match the login's, else (`deviceBinding: "enforce"`, default) `INVALID_TOKEN` and the session ends; `"flag"` only audits; `"off"` ignores |
| `fingerprint` | client-side hash of stable device attributes | a change is audited (`auth.fingerprint_changed`); browsers update, so it never blocks |
| `clientSessionId` | random id per tab or app run | recorded (latest) |
| `info` | platform, language, timezone, screen… | recorded (latest) |

A session that signed in without a `deviceId` is bound by the first refresh that sends one.
`sessionsOf` returns `device`, so a "your devices" page can show it.

**TLS fingerprint.** The server can also pass `tlsFingerprint` (JA4 or JA3) to `login` and `refresh`. It
is computed by whatever terminates TLS, so it never comes from the client: read it with security-kit's
`readTlsFingerprint` (a header set by a trusted proxy). Only its SHA-256 (`hashTlsFingerprint`) is stored,
as `Session.tlsFingerprintHash`. On refresh a different one is audited (`auth.tls_fingerprint_changed`,
with both hashes) and the latest is kept; it never blocks, because browser updates and TLS-inspecting
networks change it. A refresh without one keeps the stored hash, and `auth.device_mismatch` records
`tls: "same" | "changed" | null`, which helps tell a copied token from a cleared browser.

## API

| Call | Returns / throws |
| --- | --- |
| `login({ email, password, orgCode?, ip?, userAgent?, device?, tlsFingerprint? })` | `{ token, expiresAt, user }`, plus `refreshToken, refreshExpiresAt` in JWT mode (`token` is then the access JWT) · `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` `INVITE_PENDING` `ORG_REQUIRED` `RATE_LIMITED` |
| `refresh({ refreshToken, ip?, userAgent?, device?, tlsFingerprint? })` | JWT mode: `{ accessToken, accessExpiresAt, refreshToken, refreshExpiresAt, user }` · `INVALID_TOKEN` (also: another device) |
| `verifyAccessToken(token)` | JWT mode: claims `{ sub, org, sid, iat, exp }` or null, no storage read |
| `authenticate(token)` | `Viewer \| null` (slides the idle window) |
| `context(token)` | `{ viewer, can, branchesFor, permissions }` (anonymous when the token is missing or invalid) |
| `require(token, permission?, branchId?)` | `Viewer` · `UNAUTHENTICATED` `FORBIDDEN` |
| `logout(token)` · `logoutAll(userId, keepToken?)` | |
| `sessionsOf(userId)` · `revokeSession(userId, sessionId)` | devices; revoke one |
| `changePassword({ userId, currentPassword, newPassword, currentToken? })` | `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` `WEAK_PASSWORD` |
| `requestPasswordReset({ email, orgCode?, ip? })` | `{ token, expiresAt, user } \| null`. Deliver the token yourself; reply identically when it is null |
| `resetPassword({ token, newPassword })` | `INVALID_TOKEN` `WEAK_PASSWORD` |
| `setPassword(userId, newPassword, actorId?)` · `hashNewPassword(pw, user)` | admin tools |
| `invalidateRoles(orgId?)` | call after editing roles |

Also exported:
- `hashPassword`, `verifyPassword`, `needsRehash`, `assertPasswordPolicy`;
- `randomToken`, `hashToken`;
- `jwtSigner`, `looksLikeJwt` (HS256 sign/verify on node:crypto);
- `cleanDeviceSignals` and the `DeviceSignals` type; `hashTlsFingerprint`;
- `PERMISSIONS`, `SYSTEM_ROLES`;
- `can`, `branchesFor`, `permissionsOf`, `roleMap`.

Every failure is an `AuthError` with a stable `code`, an HTTP-style `statusCode`, and `details.retryAfterMs`
where it applies.

## Built-in roles

`owner` (everything) · `admin` · `branch_manager` · `front_desk` · `phlebotomist` · `technician` ·
`pathologist` · `accountant` (including the books: `accounts:*`) · `doctor` (referring; read only).

## Not here (by design)

- **HTTP / GraphQL endpoints.** The backend exposes `login`, `logout`, `me` and the rest as GraphQL
  mutations and queries, and calls this API.
- **Browser code.** A client package comes later.

## File: AGENTS.md

# AGENTS.md — @mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit

The backend's internal authentication API: passwords, sessions, login, reset, roles, permissions.
**No HTTP server, no GraphQL, no browser code.** The backend repo exposes these calls through its API.

## Map

```
src/password.ts  scrypt hash/verify/needsRehash, policy, randomToken, hashToken
src/jwt.ts       HS256 JWT sign/verify (node:crypto), secret rotation
src/rbac.ts      PERMISSIONS, SYSTEM_ROLES, can, branchesFor, permissionsOf, roleMap
src/stores.ts    storage interfaces (UserStore, OrgStore, RoleStore, AuditSink, SessionStore, KeyValueStore, RateLimiter)
src/memory.ts    in-process stores (tests, single server)
src/redis.ts     Redis stores ("/redis" entry): sessions, single-use values, sliding-window limiter
src/auth.ts      createAuth(): login, refresh (JWT mode), authenticate, context, require, logout, sessions, password change/reset
scripts/test.ts  128 checks; session, JWT, device-binding and TLS-fingerprint flows run on both memory and Redis (ioredis-mock) stores
```

## Rules

1. **Never store or log raw tokens.** Stores receive `hashToken(token)` only. A test asserts Redis holds no raw token.
2. **Login stays timing-safe.** An unknown email must still run one scrypt verification.
3. **Every request re-reads the user** (`authenticate`), so disabling and role changes apply at once. Do not cache users across requests.
4. Interfaces stay **structural and small**. db-kit's repositories must keep satisfying them (users, orgs, roles, audit).
5. Permissions the backend checks must exist in `PERMISSIONS` and be granted by the right `SYSTEM_ROLES`
   (db-kit's resolvers need `accounts:read|post|manage`, among others).
6. **JWT mode keeps rules 1 and 3.** Access JWTs carry the session id and every request still checks the
   session and re-reads the user; refresh tokens are opaque, single-use and stored as hashes. Never accept
   `alg` from the token (HS256 only), never sign with a secret under 32 characters.
   Device signals from clients are untrusted: always pass them through `cleanDeviceSignals`; a refresh
   from another `deviceId` ends the session unless `deviceBinding` says otherwise. The TLS fingerprint
   (`tlsFingerprint`) comes from the server (security-kit's `readTlsFingerprint`, trusted proxy only),
   never from client input; only `hashTlsFingerprint` of it is stored, and a change is audited, never blocking.
7. Error codes are a public contract (`AuthError.code`). Add new ones; never rename existing ones.

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
```

## Licence

All rights reserved (see LICENSE).

## File: llms.txt

# @mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit

> Internal authentication API for the MGPL Diagnostics backend (Node.js ≥ 20). Covers scrypt password hashing with rehash-on-login and a password policy; opaque session tokens stored as SHA-256 or (JWT mode) HS256 access tokens with rotating single-use refresh tokens, with a sliding idle timeout and an absolute max age (memory or Redis stores); timing-safe, rate-limited login with multi-organisation emails; password change and single-use reset tokens; role-based, branch-aware permissions. No HTTP server.

Key facts for agents:
- `const auth = createAuth({ users, orgs, roles, audit, sessions, kv, limiter })`. db-kit repositories satisfy users/orgs/roles/audit.
- `auth.login({ email, password, orgCode?, ip })` → `{ token, expiresAt, user }`; `auth.context(token)` → `{ viewer, can, branchesFor, permissions }`.
- Errors: `AuthError` with `code` (INVALID_CREDENTIALS, ACCOUNT_DISABLED, INVITE_PENDING, ORG_REQUIRED, RATE_LIMITED, WEAK_PASSWORD, INVALID_TOKEN, UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN) and `statusCode`.
- JWT mode: `createAuth({ …, kv, jwt: { secret, issuer?, accessTtlMs? } })`; login returns `token` (access JWT) + `refreshToken`; `auth.refresh({ refreshToken })` rotates; reuse of a spent refresh token ends the session; `verifyAccessToken` checks a JWT without storage.
- Device binding: login/refresh take `device: { deviceId, fingerprint, clientSessionId, info }`; a refresh from another deviceId → INVALID_TOKEN and the session ends (`deviceBinding: "enforce" | "flag" | "off"`); a fingerprint change is audited. `tlsFingerprint` (JA4/JA3 from the server's trusted TLS proxy, never the client) is stored only as `Session.tlsFingerprintHash`; a change is audited as auth.tls_fingerprint_changed, never blocking.
- Redis stores: `import { redisSessionStore, redisKeyValueStore, redisRateLimiter } from "@mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit/redis"`.
- Seed roles with `SYSTEM_ROLES`; permissions are "resource:action" with "*" wildcards.

## File: scripts/llms-full.mjs

````js
// Builds llms-full.txt: every doc and source file of the repo in one plain-text document for AI tools.
//   node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> [file-or-folder …]
// Folders are walked recursively. Output order: README, AGENTS, docs, then the rest alphabetically.
// Skipped: build output, dependencies, lockfiles, generated files, binaries. Files over 150 KB are
// listed (path + size) instead of inlined. CI checks the file is up to date (`npm run llms` + git diff).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { extname, join, relative } from "node:path";

const [title, ...inputs] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!title || !inputs.length) {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/llms-full.mjs "<title>" <file-or-folder> …');
  process.exit(1);
}

const TEXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".mts", ".cts", ".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".md", ".mdx", ".json", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".txt", ".graphql", ".gql", ".sql", ".html"]);
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(["node_modules", "dist", ".next", ".git", ".turbo", "coverage", "examples", ".pg-test"]);
const SKIP_FILES = /(^|\/)(package-lock\.json|pnpm-lock\.yaml|yarn\.lock|llms-full\.txt|[^/]*\.generated\.[^/]+|[^/]*\.log)$/;
const MAX = 150 * 1024;
const LANG = { ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".mts": "ts", ".cts": "ts", ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".json": "json", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml", ".graphql": "graphql", ".gql": "graphql", ".sql": "sql", ".html": "html" };

const posix = (p) => p.split("\\").join("/");
const files = new Set();
function walk(p) {
  const st = statSync(p);
  if (st.isDirectory()) {
    for (const name of readdirSync(p)) if (!SKIP_DIRS.has(name)) walk(join(p, name));
  } else if (TEXT.has(extname(p).toLowerCase()) && !SKIP_FILES.test(posix(p))) {
    files.add(posix(relative(".", p)));
  }
}
for (const input of inputs) walk(input);

const rank = (f) => (/^README\.md$/i.test(f) ? 0 : /^AGENTS\.md$/i.test(f) ? 1 : /^docs\//.test(f) ? 2 : 3);
const ordered = [...files].sort((a, b) => rank(a) - rank(b) || (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0));

const parts = [`# ${title} — full documentation and source\n\n> Generated by scripts/llms-full.mjs. Do not edit by hand. ${ordered.length} files.\n\n## Contents\n\n${ordered.map((f) => `- ${f}`).join("\n")}\n`];
const omitted = [];
for (const f of ordered) {
  // LF-normalised text, so Windows and Linux checkouts produce byte-identical output
  const body = readFileSync(f, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();
  const size = Buffer.byteLength(body);
  if (size > MAX) {
    omitted.push(`${f} (${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB)`);
    parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n_Omitted: ${(size / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB. Read the file directly._\n`);
    continue;
  }
  const lang = LANG[extname(f).toLowerCase()];
  const fence = body.includes("```") ? "````" : "```";
  parts.push(`\n\n---\n\n## File: ${f}\n\n${lang ? `${fence}${lang}\n${body}\n${fence}` : body}\n`);
}
const out = parts.join("");
writeFileSync("llms-full.txt", out);
console.log(`llms-full.txt: ${ordered.length} files, ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB${omitted.length ? `; omitted (too large): ${omitted.join(", ")}` : ""}`);
````

## File: scripts/test.ts

```ts
// npm test — passwords, login, sessions (memory + Redis stores), permissions, reset flow.
import RedisMock from "ioredis-mock";
import {
  AuthError, cleanDeviceSignals, createAuth, hashTlsFingerprint, hashPassword, hashToken, memoryKeyValueStore, memoryRateLimiter, memorySessionStore, needsRehash,
  permissionsOf, roleMap, verifyPassword, assertPasswordPolicy, can, branchesFor, SYSTEM_ROLES,
  type AuditSink, type AuthUser, type KeyValueStore, type RateLimiter, type RoleStore, type SessionStore, type UserStore,
} from "../src/index";
import { redisKeyValueStore, redisRateLimiter, redisSessionStore } from "../src/redis";

let failed = 0, passed = 0;
const ok = (cond: unknown, msg: string) => {
  if (cond) { passed++; console.log(`  ok    ${msg}`); }
  else { failed++; console.log(`  FAIL  ${msg}`); }
};
const code = async (p: Promise<unknown>) => { try { await p; return "none"; } catch (e) { return e instanceof AuthError ? e.code : `other:${(e as Error).message}`; } };
const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ in-memory stand-ins for db-kit repositories

function fakeDb() {
  const users = new Map<string, AuthUser>();
  const orgs = [{ id: "org-a", code: "MGPL" }, { id: "org-b", code: "OTHER" }];
  const orgRoles: Record<string, { key: string; permissions: string[] }[]> = { "org-a": [{ key: "lab_auditor", permissions: ["audit:read", "accounts:read"] }] };
  const auditLog: { action: string; userId?: string | null; data?: Record<string, unknown> }[] = [];
  const userStore: UserStore = {
    get: async (id) => (users.has(id) ? { ...users.get(id)! } : null),
    findByEmail: async (orgId, email) => [...users.values()].find((u) => u.orgId === orgId && u.email === email) ?? null,
    findAllByEmail: async (email) => [...users.values()].filter((u) => u.email === email),
    update: async (id, patch) => { users.set(id, { ...users.get(id)!, ...patch }); },
  };
  const roleStore: RoleStore = { find: async ({ orgId }) => orgRoles[orgId] ?? [] };
  const audit: AuditSink = { log: async (e) => { auditLog.push(e); } };
  const add = async (u: Omit<AuthUser, "passwordHash"> & { password: string; hashParams?: { N: number; r: number; p: number } }) => {
    users.set(u.id, { ...u, passwordHash: await hashPassword(u.password, u.hashParams) });
  };
  return { users, userStore, orgStore: { findOne: async ({ code }: { code: string }) => orgs.find((o) => o.code === code) ?? null }, roleStore, audit, auditLog, orgRoles, add };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ unit: passwords & RBAC

async function units() {
  console.log("\n[passwords]");
  const h = await hashPassword("correct horse battery");
  ok(h.startsWith("scrypt$32768$8$1$") && (await verifyPassword("correct horse battery", h)) && !(await verifyPassword("wrong horse", h)), "scrypt hash verifies right, rejects wrong");
  ok((await hashPassword("same")) !== (await hashPassword("same")), "salted: same password → different hashes");
  ok(needsRehash(await hashPassword("x".repeat(9), { N: 2 ** 14, r: 8, p: 1 })) && !needsRehash(h), "needsRehash spots weaker parameters");
  ok(!(await verifyPassword("a", "scrypt$99999999999$8$1$aa$bb")) && !(await verifyPassword("a", "md5$abc")), "absurd or foreign hashes are refused, not executed");
  const weak = (p: string, email?: string) => { try { assertPasswordPolicy(p, { email }); return null; } catch (e) { return (e as AuthError).code; } };
  ok(weak("short") === "WEAK_PASSWORD" && weak("password123") === "WEAK_PASSWORD" && weak("aaaaaaaaaa") === "WEAK_PASSWORD" && weak("ravi.kumar-2026", "ravi.kumar@x.in") === "WEAK_PASSWORD" && weak("tulsi-leaf-raipur") === null, "password policy: length, common, repeated, contains email");

  console.log("\n[rbac]");
  const rm = roleMap([{ key: "lab_auditor", permissions: ["audit:read"] }]);
  const desk = [{ role: "front_desk", branchId: "b1" }];
  ok(can(desk, "invoice:create", rm, "b1") && !can(desk, "invoice:create", rm, "b2") && !can(desk, "accounts:read", rm), "branch-scoped role: allowed in its branch only");
  ok(can([{ role: "owner", branchId: null }], "anything:goes", rm) && can([{ role: "admin", branchId: null }], "accounts:post", rm, "b9"), "owner *:*, admin accounts:* everywhere");
  ok(branchesFor(desk, "booking:read", rm).toString() === "b1" && branchesFor([{ role: "admin", branchId: null }], "booking:read", rm) === "all", "branchesFor: list vs all");
  ok(permissionsOf([{ role: "lab_auditor", branchId: null }], rm).join() === "audit:read", "custom organisation role");
  ok(SYSTEM_ROLES.some((r) => r.key === "accountant" && r.permissions.includes("accounts:*")), "accountant role covers the books");
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ flows, per store

async function flows(label: string, stores: { sessions: SessionStore; kv: KeyValueStore; limiter: RateLimiter }) {
  console.log(`\n[auth / ${label}]`);
  const db = fakeDb();
  await db.add({ id: "u1", orgId: "org-a", name: "Asha", email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur", status: "active", roles: [{ role: "front_desk", branchId: "b1" }] });
  await db.add({ id: "u2", orgId: "org-a", name: "Old", email: "old@mgpl.in", password: "neem-tree-arang", status: "active", roles: [{ role: "owner", branchId: null }], hashParams: { N: 2 ** 14, r: 8, p: 1 } });
  await db.add({ id: "u3", orgId: "org-a", name: "Gone", email: "gone@mgpl.in", password: "mango-season-27", status: "disabled", roles: [] });
  await db.add({ id: "u4", orgId: "org-a", name: "Dual A", email: "dual@x.in", password: "shared-pass-99", status: "active", roles: [{ role: "owner", branchId: null }] });
  await db.add({ id: "u5", orgId: "org-b", name: "Dual B", email: "dual@x.in", password: "shared-pass-99", status: "active", roles: [{ role: "owner", branchId: null }] });
  const auth = createAuth({
    users: db.userStore, orgs: db.orgStore, roles: db.roleStore, audit: db.audit, ...stores,
    session: { idleMs: 60_000, maxAgeMs: 120_000, touchEveryMs: 0 },
  });

  const login = await auth.login({ email: "  ASHA@mgpl.in ", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur", ip: "1.1.1.1", userAgent: "test" });
  ok(login.token.length === 43 && login.user.email === "asha@mgpl.in" && !("passwordHash" in login.user), "login: token issued, email normalised, no hash returned");
  const v = await auth.authenticate(login.token);
  ok(v?.userId === "u1" && v.orgId === "org-a" && v.sessionId === hashToken(login.token), "authenticate: token → viewer");
  ok((await code(auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "wrong-password" }))) === "INVALID_CREDENTIALS", "wrong password → INVALID_CREDENTIALS");
  ok((await code(auth.login({ email: "nobody@mgpl.in", password: "whatever-pass" }))) === "INVALID_CREDENTIALS", "unknown email → same INVALID_CREDENTIALS");

  let t = Date.now(); await code(auth.login({ email: "nobody2@mgpl.in", password: "whatever-pass" })); const unknownMs = Date.now() - t;
  t = Date.now(); await code(auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "whatever-pass" })); const wrongMs = Date.now() - t;
  ok(unknownMs > wrongMs * 0.4, `timing-safe: unknown email ${unknownMs} ms vs wrong password ${wrongMs} ms`);

  ok((await code(auth.login({ email: "gone@mgpl.in", password: "mango-season-27" }))) === "ACCOUNT_DISABLED", "disabled account → ACCOUNT_DISABLED");
  ok((await code(auth.login({ email: "dual@x.in", password: "shared-pass-99" }))) === "ORG_REQUIRED", "same email in two organisations → ORG_REQUIRED");
  ok((await auth.login({ email: "dual@x.in", password: "shared-pass-99", orgCode: "other" })).user.id === "u5", "…with orgCode → the right one");

  const before = db.users.get("u2")!.passwordHash;
  await auth.login({ email: "old@mgpl.in", password: "neem-tree-arang" });
  ok(before.startsWith("scrypt$16384$") && db.users.get("u2")!.passwordHash.startsWith("scrypt$32768$"), "weak hash upgraded on login");

  // context & permissions
  const ctx = await auth.context(login.token);
  ok(ctx.can("invoice:create", "b1") && !ctx.can("invoice:create", "b2") && !ctx.can("accounts:read") && ctx.branchesFor("booking:read").toString() === "b1", "context: branch-aware can / branchesFor");
  db.users.set("u1", { ...db.users.get("u1")!, roles: [{ role: "lab_auditor", branchId: null }] });
  ok((await auth.context(login.token)).can("accounts:read"), "role change applies on the next request (custom org role)");
  db.orgRoles["org-a"] = [{ key: "lab_auditor", permissions: ["audit:read"] }];
  auth.invalidateRoles("org-a");
  ok(!(await auth.context(login.token)).can("accounts:read"), "invalidateRoles: edited role applies at once");
  ok((await code(auth.require(login.token, "settings:manage"))) === "FORBIDDEN" && (await code(auth.require("bad-token-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"))) === "UNAUTHENTICATED", "require: FORBIDDEN / UNAUTHENTICATED");
  const anon = await auth.context(null);
  ok(anon.viewer === null && !anon.can("patient:read"), "anonymous context can nothing");

  // sessions
  const second = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur", userAgent: "phone" });
  ok((await auth.sessionsOf("u1")).length === 2 && (await auth.revokeSession("u1", hashToken(second.token))) && (await auth.authenticate(second.token)) === null, "two devices listed; one revoked by id");
  // idle timeout, with its own short window (logins themselves take ~100 ms of scrypt)
  const short = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, ...stores, session: { idleMs: 500, maxAgeMs: 60_000, touchEveryMs: 0 } });
  const busy = await short.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  const idle = await short.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  await sleep(300);
  await short.authenticate(busy.token); // used: slides its window
  await sleep(300);
  ok((await short.authenticate(busy.token)) !== null && (await short.authenticate(idle.token)) === null, "idle timeout: used session slides, unused one expires");
  const capped = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, ...stores, session: { idleMs: 60_000, maxAgeMs: 300, touchEveryMs: 0 } });
  const c = await capped.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  await sleep(350);
  ok((await capped.authenticate(c.token)) === null, "absolute max age ends even an active session");
  db.users.set("u1", { ...db.users.get("u1")!, status: "disabled" });
  ok((await auth.authenticate(login.token)) === null && (await auth.sessionsOf("u1")).length === 0, "disabling a user ends their sessions at once");
  db.users.set("u1", { ...db.users.get("u1")!, status: "active" });

  const s1 = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  const s2 = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  await auth.logout(s1.token);
  ok((await auth.authenticate(s1.token)) === null && (await auth.authenticate(s2.token)) !== null, "logout ends only that session");
  ok((await code(auth.changePassword({ userId: "u1", currentPassword: "nope-nope-nope", newPassword: "banyan-roots-7" }))) === "INVALID_CREDENTIALS", "change password needs the current one");
  const s3 = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  await auth.changePassword({ userId: "u1", currentPassword: "tulsi-leaf-raipur", newPassword: "banyan-roots-7", currentToken: s3.token });
  ok((await auth.authenticate(s3.token)) !== null && (await auth.authenticate(s2.token)) === null, "change password keeps this session, ends the others");

  // reset
  ok((await auth.requestPasswordReset({ email: "ghost@mgpl.in" })) === null, "reset for unknown email → null (respond the same either way)");
  const r = (await auth.requestPasswordReset({ email: "asha@mgpl.in" }))!;
  await auth.resetPassword({ token: r.token, newPassword: "peepal-shade-12" });
  ok((await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "peepal-shade-12" })).user.id === "u1" && (await auth.authenticate(s3.token)) === null, "reset sets the password and ends every session");
  ok((await code(auth.resetPassword({ token: r.token, newPassword: "another-one-55" }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN", "reset token is single-use");
  ok((await code(auth.resetPassword({ token: (await auth.requestPasswordReset({ email: "asha@mgpl.in" }))!.token, newPassword: "short" }))) === "WEAK_PASSWORD", "reset enforces the password policy");

  // rate limit (fresh limiter: 3 attempts / window)
  const strict = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, sessions: stores.sessions, limiter: label === "redis" ? redisRateLimiter(new RedisMock() as any, { limit: 3, windowMs: 60_000, prefix: `rl${Date.now()}:` }) : memoryRateLimiter({ limit: 3, windowMs: 60_000 }) });
  const codes: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) codes.push(await code(strict.login({ email: "old@mgpl.in", password: "bad-guess-000", ip: "9.9.9.9" })));
  ok(codes.slice(0, 3).every((c) => c === "INVALID_CREDENTIALS") && codes[3] === "RATE_LIMITED", "4th attempt from the same IP/email → RATE_LIMITED");
  const office = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, sessions: stores.sessions, limiter: label === "redis" ? redisRateLimiter(new RedisMock() as any, { limit: 3, windowMs: 60_000, prefix: `rlo${Date.now()}:` }) : memoryRateLimiter({ limit: 3, windowMs: 60_000 }) });
  let signedIn = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) if ((await office.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "peepal-shade-12", ip: "7.7.7.7" })).user) signedIn++;
  const guesses: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) guesses.push(await code(office.login({ email: `nobody${i}@mgpl.in`, password: "bad-guess-000", ip: "7.7.7.7" })));
  ok(signedIn === 6 && guesses.slice(0, 3).every((c) => c === "INVALID_CREDENTIALS") && guesses[3] === "RATE_LIMITED", "successful logins do not use up the IP's limit (shared office connection); failures still do");

  ok(db.auditLog.some((e) => e.action === "auth.login") && db.auditLog.some((e) => e.action === "auth.login_failed") && db.auditLog.some((e) => e.action === "auth.password_reset"), "audit trail written");
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ JWT mode: access + refresh tokens

const SECRET = "test-secret-0123456789-abcdefghijklmnop";
const issued: string[] = []; // refresh tokens handed out, to prove Redis never stores them

async function jwtFlows(label: string, stores: { sessions: SessionStore; kv: KeyValueStore; limiter: RateLimiter }) {
  console.log(`\n[jwt / ${label}]`);
  const db = fakeDb();
  await db.add({ id: "j1", orgId: "org-a", name: "Asha", email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur", status: "active", roles: [{ role: "front_desk", branchId: "b1" }] });
  const auth = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, audit: db.audit, ...stores, session: { idleMs: 60_000, maxAgeMs: 120_000, touchEveryMs: 0 }, jwt: { secret: SECRET, issuer: "mgpl-api", accessTtlMs: 60_000, reuseGraceMs: 200 } });

  const l = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  issued.push(l.refreshToken!);
  const [h, p] = l.token.split(".");
  const header = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(h!, "base64url").toString());
  const claims = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(p!, "base64url").toString());
  ok(header.alg === "HS256" && claims.sub === "j1" && claims.org === "org-a" && claims.iss === "mgpl-api" && claims.exp - claims.iat === 60, "login: HS256 access JWT (sub, org, sid, iss, 60 s)");
  ok(!!l.refreshToken && l.refreshToken.length === 43 && l.refreshExpiresAt! > l.expiresAt, "login: opaque refresh token outlives the access token");
  ok((await auth.authenticate(l.token))?.userId === "j1" && auth.verifyAccessToken(l.token)?.sid === claims.sid, "access token → viewer; verifyAccessToken without storage");
  ok((await auth.authenticate(l.refreshToken)) === null, "a refresh token is not a bearer token");

  // tampering
  const forged = `${h}.${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ ...claims, sub: "someone-else" })).toString("base64url")}.${l.token.split(".")[2]}`;
  const none = `${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ alg: "none", typ: "JWT" })).toString("base64url")}.${p}.`;
  const other = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, ...stores, jwt: { secret: "another-secret-0123456789-abcdefghijk" } });
  ok((await auth.authenticate(forged)) === null && (await auth.authenticate(none)) === null && (await other.authenticate(l.token)) === null, "forged claims, alg none and a foreign secret are refused");
  const rotated = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, ...stores, jwt: { secret: ["new-secret-0123456789-abcdefghijklmnopq", SECRET], issuer: "mgpl-api" } });
  ok((await rotated.authenticate(l.token))?.userId === "j1", "secret rotation: old tokens verify while the old secret is listed");

  // refresh rotation
  const r1 = await auth.refresh({ refreshToken: l.refreshToken! });
  issued.push(r1.refreshToken);
  ok(r1.refreshToken !== l.refreshToken && (await auth.authenticate(r1.accessToken))?.userId === "j1" && auth.verifyAccessToken(r1.accessToken)?.sid === claims.sid, "refresh: new access + new refresh token, same session");
  ok((await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: l.refreshToken! }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN" && (await auth.authenticate(r1.accessToken)) !== null, "spent refresh token within the grace window: refused, session kept");
  await sleep(250);
  ok((await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: l.refreshToken! }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN" && (await auth.authenticate(r1.accessToken)) === null, "spent refresh token reused later: session ended (theft)");
  ok((await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: r1.refreshToken }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN" && db.auditLog.some((e) => e.action === "auth.refresh_reuse"), "…its newer refresh token dies too, and it is audited");

  // logout / revocation apply at once despite a valid signature
  const a = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  const b = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  issued.push(a.refreshToken!, b.refreshToken!);
  await auth.logout(a.token);
  ok((await auth.authenticate(a.token)) === null && (await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: a.refreshToken! }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN" && (await auth.authenticate(b.token)) !== null, "logout with the access token ends that session and its refresh token");
  await auth.logout(b.refreshToken!);
  ok((await auth.authenticate(b.token)) === null, "logout with the refresh token works too");
  const c = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  const d = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "tulsi-leaf-raipur" });
  issued.push(c.refreshToken!, d.refreshToken!);
  await auth.changePassword({ userId: "j1", currentPassword: "tulsi-leaf-raipur", newPassword: "banyan-roots-7", currentToken: c.token });
  ok((await auth.authenticate(c.token)) !== null && (await auth.authenticate(d.token)) === null, "change password with an access token keeps this session only");
  db.users.set("j1", { ...db.users.get("j1")!, status: "disabled" });
  ok((await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: c.refreshToken! }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN" && (await auth.authenticate(c.token)) === null, "disabled user: refresh refused, access token dead at once");

  const expiring = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, ...stores, jwt: { secret: SECRET, accessTtlMs: 1000 } });
  db.users.set("j1", { ...db.users.get("j1")!, status: "active" });
  const e = await expiring.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "banyan-roots-7" });
  issued.push(e.refreshToken!);
  await sleep(1100);
  ok((await expiring.authenticate(e.token)) === null && (await expiring.authenticate((await expiring.refresh({ refreshToken: e.refreshToken! })).accessToken)) !== null, "expired access token refused; refresh brings a working one");
  // device binding: the refresh token works only on the device that signed in
  const phone = { deviceId: "dev-phone-0001-abcdef", fingerprint: "fp-aaaaaaaaaaaa", clientSessionId: "tab-0001-xyz", info: { platform: "Android", screen: "412x915", "bad key": "x", note: "y".repeat(500) } };
  const f = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "banyan-roots-7", device: phone as any });
  issued.push(f.refreshToken!);
  const stored = (await auth.sessionsOf("j1")).find((x) => x.id === auth.verifyAccessToken(f.token)?.sid);
  ok(stored?.device?.deviceId === phone.deviceId && stored.device.info?.platform === "Android" && !("bad key" in (stored.device.info ?? {})) && String(stored.device.info?.note).length === 200, "login stores the device signals on the session (cleaned, capped)");
  const f2 = await auth.refresh({ refreshToken: f.refreshToken!, device: { ...phone, fingerprint: "fp-bbbbbbbbbbbb" } });
  issued.push(f2.refreshToken);
  ok(!!f2.accessToken && db.auditLog.some((x) => x.action === "auth.fingerprint_changed"), "same device, new fingerprint: refresh works, change audited");
  ok((await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: f2.refreshToken, device: { deviceId: "dev-laptop-9999-zzzzzz" } }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN" && (await auth.authenticate(f2.accessToken)) === null && db.auditLog.some((x) => x.action === "auth.device_mismatch"), "refresh from another device: refused, session ended, audited");
  const g = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "banyan-roots-7", device: phone });
  issued.push(g.refreshToken!);
  ok((await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: g.refreshToken! }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN", "refresh without the device id of a bound session: refused");
  const flagging = createAuth({ users: db.userStore, audit: db.audit, ...stores, deviceBinding: "flag", jwt: { secret: SECRET } });
  const h2 = await flagging.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "banyan-roots-7", device: phone });
  issued.push(h2.refreshToken!);
  const h3 = await flagging.refresh({ refreshToken: h2.refreshToken!, device: { deviceId: "dev-laptop-9999-zzzzzz" } });
  issued.push(h3.refreshToken);
  ok(!!h3.accessToken, 'deviceBinding "flag": a refresh from another device works (and is audited)');
  ok(cleanDeviceSignals({ deviceId: "short", fingerprint: "<script>alert(1)</script>xx" }) === undefined, "malformed device ids are dropped");

  // TLS fingerprint (from the proxy, server side): stored hashed, a change is audited, never blocking
  const JA4 = "t13d1516h2_8daaf6152771_e5627efa2ab1", JA4b = "t13d1517h2_8daaf6152771_b1ff8ab2d16f";
  const t = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "banyan-roots-7", device: phone, tlsFingerprint: JA4 });
  issued.push(t.refreshToken!, JA4, JA4b);
  const sidOf = (tok: string) => auth.verifyAccessToken(tok)?.sid;
  const tStored = (await auth.sessionsOf("j1")).find((x) => x.id === sidOf(t.token));
  ok(tStored?.tlsFingerprintHash === hashTlsFingerprint(JA4) && tStored?.tlsFingerprintHash !== JA4 && !JSON.stringify(tStored).includes(JA4), "login stores the TLS fingerprint as a hash only");
  const before = db.auditLog.length;
  const t2 = await auth.refresh({ refreshToken: t.refreshToken!, device: phone, tlsFingerprint: JA4 });
  ok(!db.auditLog.slice(before).some((x) => x.action === "auth.tls_fingerprint_changed"), "same TLS fingerprint: nothing audited");
  const t3 = await auth.refresh({ refreshToken: t2.refreshToken, device: phone, tlsFingerprint: JA4b });
  issued.push(t2.refreshToken, t3.refreshToken);
  const tlsAudit = db.auditLog.find((x) => x.action === "auth.tls_fingerprint_changed");
  ok(!!t3.accessToken && tlsAudit?.data?.from === hashTlsFingerprint(JA4) && tlsAudit?.data?.to === hashTlsFingerprint(JA4b), "new TLS fingerprint: refresh works, change audited (hashes)");
  ok((await auth.sessionsOf("j1")).find((x) => x.id === sidOf(t3.accessToken))?.tlsFingerprintHash === hashTlsFingerprint(JA4b), "the session records the latest TLS fingerprint hash");
  const t4 = await auth.refresh({ refreshToken: t3.refreshToken, device: phone });
  issued.push(t4.refreshToken);
  ok((await auth.sessionsOf("j1")).find((x) => x.id === sidOf(t4.accessToken))?.tlsFingerprintHash === hashTlsFingerprint(JA4b), "a refresh without a TLS fingerprint (TLS ended elsewhere) keeps the stored one");
  const u = await auth.login({ email: "asha@mgpl.in", password: "banyan-roots-7", device: phone });
  issued.push(u.refreshToken!);
  const u2 = await auth.refresh({ refreshToken: u.refreshToken!, device: phone, tlsFingerprint: JA4 });
  issued.push(u2.refreshToken);
  ok((await auth.sessionsOf("j1")).find((x) => x.id === sidOf(u2.accessToken))?.tlsFingerprintHash === hashTlsFingerprint(JA4), "a session without one is bound by the first refresh that has one");
  ok((await code(auth.refresh({ refreshToken: t4.refreshToken, device: { deviceId: "dev-laptop-9999-zzzzzz" }, tlsFingerprint: JA4b }))) === "INVALID_TOKEN" && db.auditLog.some((x) => x.action === "auth.device_mismatch" && x.data?.tls === "same"), "a device mismatch audit says whether the TLS fingerprint matched");
  ok(hashTlsFingerprint("has space x") === undefined && hashTlsFingerprint("short") === undefined && hashTlsFingerprint("x".repeat(257)) === undefined, "malformed TLS fingerprints are dropped");

  let threw = false;
  try { createAuth({ users: db.userStore, sessions: stores.sessions, jwt: { secret: "short" } }); } catch { threw = true; }
  ok(threw, "JWT mode refuses short secrets and a missing kv");
}

async function main() {
  const t0 = Date.now();
  await units();
  await flows("memory", { sessions: memorySessionStore(), kv: memoryKeyValueStore(), limiter: memoryRateLimiter({ limit: 100, windowMs: 60_000 }) });
  const redis = new RedisMock() as any;
  await flows("redis", { sessions: redisSessionStore(redis), kv: redisKeyValueStore(redis), limiter: redisRateLimiter(redis, { limit: 100, windowMs: 60_000 }) });
  await jwtFlows("memory", { sessions: memorySessionStore(), kv: memoryKeyValueStore(), limiter: memoryRateLimiter({ limit: 100, windowMs: 60_000 }) });
  await jwtFlows("redis", { sessions: redisSessionStore(redis), kv: redisKeyValueStore(redis), limiter: redisRateLimiter(redis, { limit: 100, windowMs: 60_000 }) });
  const dump = (await Promise.all(((await redis.keys("*")) as string[]).map(async (k) => `${k} ${(await redis.type(k)) === "string" ? await redis.get(k) : ""}`))).join("\n");
  ok(issued.length > 5 && issued.every((t) => !dump.includes(t)), "redis never holds a raw refresh token");
  const keys: string[] = await redis.keys("*");
  ok(keys.length > 0 && !keys.some((k) => /[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(k) && !k.includes("sess:") && !k.includes("kv:")), "redis holds token hashes only");
  redis.disconnect();
  console.log(`\n${passed} passed, ${failed} failed in ${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`);
  process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
}

main().catch((e) => { console.error(e); process.exit(1); });
```

## File: src/auth.ts

```ts
import { AuthError } from "./errors";
import { jwtSigner, looksLikeJwt, type AccessClaims, type JwtOptions } from "./jwt";
import { memoryRateLimiter } from "./memory";
import { assertPasswordPolicy, hashPassword, hashToken, needsRehash, randomToken, verifyPassword, type PasswordPolicy } from "./password";
import { branchesFor, can, permissionsOf, roleMap, type Permission, type RoleAssignment, type RoleMap } from "./rbac";
import type { AuditSink, AuthUser, DeviceSignals, KeyValueStore, OrgStore, RateLimiter, RoleStore, Session, SessionStore, UserStore } from "./stores";

export interface AuthOptions {
  users: UserStore;
  sessions: SessionStore;
  /** Needed for login with an organisation code. */
  orgs?: OrgStore;
  /** The organisation's own roles; without it only SYSTEM_ROLES apply. */
  roles?: RoleStore;
  audit?: AuditSink;
  /** Needed for password reset. */
  kv?: KeyValueStore;
  /** Login / reset attempts per IP and per email. Default: 10 per 15 minutes per key, in memory. */
  limiter?: RateLimiter;
  session?: {
    /** Logged out after this long without use. Default 12 h. */
    idleMs?: number;
    /** Logged out after this long regardless. Default 30 days. */
    maxAgeMs?: number;
    /** Extend the idle window at most this often (saves writes). Default 60 s. */
    touchEveryMs?: number;
  };
  /** Password-reset link lifetime. Default 30 minutes. */
  resetTtlMs?: number;
  /** How long an organisation's role list is cached. Default 30 s. */
  roleCacheMs?: number;
  passwordPolicy?: PasswordPolicy;
  /**
   * JWT mode: login and refresh return a short-lived access token (HS256 JWT, sent as Bearer) and a
   * long-lived, single-use refresh token (opaque, rotated on every refresh). Needs `kv`. Without it,
   * login returns one opaque session token as before.
   */
  jwt?: JwtOptions & {
    /** Access-token lifetime. Default 15 minutes. */
    accessTtlMs?: number;
    /**
     * A refresh token used twice is a theft signal and ends its session. Within this window the second
     * use only fails (two tabs refreshing at once). Default 15 s.
     */
    reuseGraceMs?: number;
  };
  /**
   * What a refresh from another device does. The device is the `deviceId` the client sent at login.
   * "enforce" (default): refused with INVALID_TOKEN and the session ends (audit auth.device_mismatch).
   * "flag": allowed, audited. "off": not compared. A changed fingerprint is only audited (auth.fingerprint_changed),
   * and so is a changed TLS fingerprint (auth.tls_fingerprint_changed).
   */
  deviceBinding?: "enforce" | "flag" | "off";
}

/** The signed-in user for one request. */
export interface Viewer {
  userId: string;
  orgId: string;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  roles: RoleAssignment[];
  sessionId: string;
}

/** What a request handler needs: who is calling and what they may do (fits db-kit's GraphQL context). */
export interface AuthContext {
  viewer: Viewer | null;
  can(permission: string, branchId?: string | null): boolean;
  branchesFor(permission: string): "all" | string[];
  permissions(branchId?: string | null): Permission[];
}

export type PublicUser = Omit<AuthUser, "passwordHash">;

export interface LoginInput {
  email: string;
  password: string;
  /** Required only when the same email/password exists in several organisations. */
  orgCode?: string;
  ip?: string;
  userAgent?: string;
  /** Security signals from the client (device id, fingerprint, …), stored on the session. */
  device?: DeviceSignals;
  /**
   * TLS client fingerprint (JA4 / JA3) from the TLS-terminating proxy (security-kit's readTlsFingerprint),
   * never from client input. Only its hash is stored (`Session.tlsFingerprintHash`).
   */
  tlsFingerprint?: string;
}

export interface LoginResult {
  /**
   * Give this to the client (Authorization: Bearer … or an httpOnly cookie). It is never stored.
   * In JWT mode it is the access token and `expiresAt` its expiry.
   */
  token: string;
  expiresAt: Date;
  user: PublicUser;
  /** JWT mode only: single-use, rotated by `refresh`. Only its hash is stored. */
  refreshToken?: string;
  /** JWT mode only: the refresh token dies here unless used before (idle window, session max age). */
  refreshExpiresAt?: Date;
}

/** What `refresh` returns: a new access token and the next refresh token (the old one is spent). */
export interface TokenPair {
  accessToken: string;
  accessExpiresAt: Date;
  refreshToken: string;
  refreshExpiresAt: Date;
  user: PublicUser;
}

const publicUser = ({ passwordHash: _p, ...u }: AuthUser): PublicUser => u;
const normalizeEmail = (e: string) => e.trim().toLowerCase();

const ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:+\/=-]{8,128}$/;
/** Keeps only well-formed, size-capped device signals (clients are untrusted). */
export function cleanDeviceSignals(d: DeviceSignals | null | undefined): DeviceSignals | undefined {
  if (!d || typeof d !== "object") return undefined;
  const out: DeviceSignals = {};
  for (const k of ["deviceId", "fingerprint", "clientSessionId"] as const) {
    const v = d[k];
    if (typeof v === "string" && ID_RE.test(v)) out[k] = v;
  }
  if (d.info && typeof d.info === "object" && !Array.isArray(d.info)) {
    const info: Record<string, string | number | boolean> = {};
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(d.info).slice(0, 20)) {
      if (!/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}$/.test(k)) continue;
      if (typeof v === "string") info[k] = v.slice(0, 200);
      else if ((typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v)) || typeof v === "boolean") info[k] = v;
    }
    if (Object.keys(info).length) out.info = info;
  }
  return Object.keys(out).length ? out : undefined;
}

const TLS_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:,+\/=-]{8,256}$/;
/** SHA-256 of a well-formed TLS fingerprint, or undefined. The fingerprint itself is never stored. */
export function hashTlsFingerprint(v: string | null | undefined): string | undefined {
  return typeof v === "string" && TLS_RE.test(v) ? hashToken(v) : undefined;
}

export type Auth = ReturnType<typeof createAuth>;

/**
 * The backend's internal auth API. No HTTP: call it from GraphQL resolvers, REST handlers, jobs.
 *
 *   const auth = createAuth({ users: db.repos.users, orgs: db.repos.orgs, roles: db.repos.roles,
 *                             audit: db.repos.audit, sessions: redisSessionStore(redis), kv: redisKeyValueStore(redis),
 *                             limiter: redisRateLimiter(redis, { limit: 10, windowMs: 15 * 60_000 }) });
 *   const { token } = await auth.login({ email, password, ip });
 *   const ctx = await auth.context(token);      // { viewer, can, branchesFor, permissions }
 */
export function createAuth(o: AuthOptions) {
  const idleMs = o.session?.idleMs ?? 12 * 3600_000;
  const maxAgeMs = o.session?.maxAgeMs ?? 30 * 86400_000;
  const touchEveryMs = o.session?.touchEveryMs ?? 60_000;
  const resetTtlMs = o.resetTtlMs ?? 30 * 60_000;
  const roleCacheMs = o.roleCacheMs ?? 30_000;
  const limiter = o.limiter ?? memoryRateLimiter({ limit: 10, windowMs: 15 * 60_000 });
  const roleCache = new Map<string, { map: RoleMap; at: number }>();
  let dummy: Promise<string> | undefined;
  const jwt = o.jwt ? jwtSigner(o.jwt) : null;
  const accessTtlMs = o.jwt?.accessTtlMs ?? 15 * 60_000;
  const reuseGraceMs = o.jwt?.reuseGraceMs ?? 15_000;
  if (jwt && !o.kv) throw new Error("createAuth: JWT mode needs `kv` (refresh tokens)");
  const deviceBinding = o.deviceBinding ?? "enforce";

  const audit = async (entry: Parameters<AuditSink["log"]>[0]) => {
    try {
      await o.audit?.log(entry);
    } catch {
      /* auditing must never break a login */
    }
  };

  async function limit(keys: (string | undefined)[]) {
    for (const k of keys) {
      if (!k) continue;
      const r = await limiter.hit(k);
      if (!r.allowed) throw new AuthError("RATE_LIMITED", "Too many attempts. Try again later.", { retryAfterMs: r.retryAfterMs });
    }
  }

  async function findCandidates(email: string, orgCode?: string): Promise<AuthUser[]> {
    if (!orgCode) return o.users.findAllByEmail(email);
    if (!o.orgs) throw new Error("createAuth: pass `orgs` to log in with an organisation code");
    const org = await o.orgs.findOne({ code: orgCode.trim().toUpperCase() });
    const user = org ? await o.users.findByEmail(org.id, email) : null;
    return user ? [user] : [];
  }

  async function startSession(user: AuthUser, ip?: string, userAgent?: string, device?: DeviceSignals, tlsFingerprint?: string): Promise<{ token: string; session: Session }> {
    const token = randomToken();
    const now = Date.now();
    // JWT mode: the session id is random and never handed out; the refresh token points at it through kv
    const id = jwt ? hashToken(randomToken()) : hashToken(token);
    const session: Session = { id, userId: user.id, orgId: user.orgId, createdAt: now, lastSeenAt: now, expiresAt: now + maxAgeMs, ip, userAgent, device: cleanDeviceSignals(device), tlsFingerprintHash: hashTlsFingerprint(tlsFingerprint) };
    await o.sessions.create(session, idleMs);
    if (jwt) await o.kv!.set(`refresh:${hashToken(token)}`, id, maxAgeMs);
    return { token, session };
  }

  /** A signed access token for a session (JWT mode). */
  function accessToken(s: Session): { token: string; expiresAt: Date } {
    const now = Date.now();
    const exp = Math.min(now + accessTtlMs, s.expiresAt);
    return { token: jwt!.sign({ sub: s.userId, org: s.orgId, sid: s.id, iat: Math.floor(now / 1000), exp: Math.floor(exp / 1000) }), expiresAt: new Date(Math.floor(exp / 1000) * 1000) };
  }

  const refreshExpiry = (s: Session, now = Date.now()) => new Date(Math.min(s.expiresAt, now + idleMs));

  /** The session a token belongs to: an access JWT's `sid` (expired ones too), else the opaque token's hash. */
  function sessionIdOf(token: string): string | null {
    if (jwt && looksLikeJwt(token)) return jwt.verify(token, { ignoreExpiry: true })?.sid ?? null;
    return hashToken(token);
  }

  async function rolesFor(orgId: string): Promise<RoleMap> {
    const hit = roleCache.get(orgId);
    if (hit && Date.now() - hit.at < roleCacheMs) return hit.map;
    const map = roleMap(o.roles ? await o.roles.find({ orgId }) : []);
    roleCache.set(orgId, { map, at: Date.now() });
    return map;
  }

  async function authenticate(token: string | null | undefined): Promise<Viewer | null> {
    if (!token || token.length < 20) return null;
    let s: Session | null;
    if (jwt && looksLikeJwt(token)) {
      const claims = jwt.verify(token);
      if (!claims) return null;
      // the session is still checked, so logout, revocation and "log out everywhere" apply at once
      s = await o.sessions.get(claims.sid);
      if (!s || s.userId !== claims.sub) return null;
    } else {
      if (token.length > 200) return null;
      s = await o.sessions.get(hashToken(token));
    }
    if (!s) return null;
    // the user is read on every request, so disabling an account or changing roles applies immediately
    const user = await o.users.get(s.userId);
    if (!user || user.status !== "active") {
      await o.sessions.deleteByUser(s.userId); // disabled or deleted: end every device at once
      return null;
    }
    if (user.orgId !== s.orgId) {
      await o.sessions.delete(s.id);
      return null;
    }
    const now = Date.now();
    if (now - s.lastSeenAt >= touchEveryMs) await o.sessions.touch(s.id, now, idleMs);
    return { userId: user.id, orgId: user.orgId, name: user.name, email: user.email, roles: user.roles, sessionId: s.id };
  }

  async function setNewPassword(user: AuthUser, newPassword: string, keepSessionId?: string) {
    assertPasswordPolicy(newPassword, { email: user.email, name: user.name }, o.passwordPolicy);
    await o.users.update(user.id, { passwordHash: await hashPassword(newPassword) });
    await o.sessions.deleteByUser(user.id, keepSessionId);
  }

  return {
    /** Email + password → session token. Timing-safe, rate-limited, audited. */
    async login(input: LoginInput): Promise<LoginResult> {
      const email = normalizeEmail(input.email);
      await limit([input.ip && `login:ip:${input.ip}`, `login:email:${email}`]);
      const candidates = await findCandidates(email, input.orgCode);
      // unknown email still costs one scrypt verification, so its timing matches a wrong password
      if (!candidates.length) await verifyPassword(input.password, await (dummy ??= hashPassword(randomToken())));
      const matched: AuthUser[] = [];
      for (const u of candidates) if (await verifyPassword(input.password, u.passwordHash)) matched.push(u);
      if (!matched.length) {
        const first = candidates[0];
        if (first) await audit({ orgId: first.orgId, userId: first.id, action: "auth.login_failed", ip: input.ip });
        throw new AuthError("INVALID_CREDENTIALS", "Email or password is incorrect");
      }
      if (matched.length > 1) throw new AuthError("ORG_REQUIRED", "This email belongs to several organisations. Choose one.");
      const user = matched[0]!;
      if (user.status === "disabled") throw new AuthError("ACCOUNT_DISABLED", "This account is disabled");
      if (user.status === "invited") throw new AuthError("INVITE_PENDING", "Accept your invitation first");

      await limiter.reset(`login:email:${email}`);
      // only failed attempts count against the IP: staff behind one office connection must all be able to
      // sign in. Every attempt is still counted first, so a burst of guesses is blocked before verification.
      if (input.ip) await limiter.undo?.(`login:ip:${input.ip}`);
      const patch: { lastLoginAt: Date; passwordHash?: string } = { lastLoginAt: new Date() };
      if (needsRehash(user.passwordHash)) patch.passwordHash = await hashPassword(input.password);
      await o.users.update(user.id, patch);
      const { token, session } = await startSession(user, input.ip, input.userAgent, input.device, input.tlsFingerprint);
      await audit({ orgId: user.orgId, userId: user.id, action: "auth.login", ip: input.ip });
      const pub = publicUser({ ...user, lastLoginAt: patch.lastLoginAt });
      if (!jwt) return { token, expiresAt: new Date(session.expiresAt), user: pub };
      const access = accessToken(session);
      return { token: access.token, expiresAt: access.expiresAt, refreshToken: token, refreshExpiresAt: refreshExpiry(session), user: pub };
    },

    /**
     * JWT mode: spends a refresh token and returns a new access token and the next refresh token.
     * Fails with INVALID_TOKEN when the token is unknown, spent, expired, or its session or user is
     * gone. A spent token presented again after `reuseGraceMs` ends the whole session (it was copied).
     */
    async refresh(input: { refreshToken: string; ip?: string; userAgent?: string; device?: DeviceSignals; tlsFingerprint?: string }): Promise<TokenPair> {
      if (!jwt) throw new Error("createAuth: refresh needs the `jwt` option");
      const invalid = () => new AuthError("INVALID_TOKEN", "Sign in again");
      const rt = input.refreshToken ?? "";
      if (rt.length < 20 || rt.length > 200) throw invalid();
      const h = hashToken(rt);
      const now = Date.now();
      const sid = await o.kv!.take(`refresh:${h}`);
      if (!sid) {
        const used = await o.kv!.take(`refresh-used:${h}`);
        if (used) {
          const [usedSid, at] = used.split("|");
          if (now - Number(at) <= reuseGraceMs) {
            await o.kv!.set(`refresh-used:${h}`, used, maxAgeMs); // keep the marker for later reuse
          } else if (usedSid) {
            const s = await o.sessions.get(usedSid);
            await o.sessions.delete(usedSid);
            if (s) await audit({ orgId: s.orgId, userId: s.userId, action: "auth.refresh_reuse", ip: input.ip });
          }
        }
        throw invalid();
      }
      const s = await o.sessions.get(sid);
      if (!s) throw invalid();
      const user = await o.users.get(s.userId);
      if (!user || user.status !== "active" || user.orgId !== s.orgId) {
        await o.sessions.deleteByUser(s.userId);
        throw invalid();
      }
      // device binding: the refresh token only works on the device that signed in
      const device = cleanDeviceSignals(input.device);
      const bound = s.device?.deviceId;
      // TLS fingerprint (server side, hashed): "same" / "changed", or null when either side has none
      const tls = hashTlsFingerprint(input.tlsFingerprint);
      const tlsVerdict = tls && s.tlsFingerprintHash ? (tls === s.tlsFingerprintHash ? "same" : "changed") : null;
      let session = s;
      if (deviceBinding !== "off" && bound && device?.deviceId !== bound) {
        await audit({ orgId: s.orgId, userId: s.userId, action: "auth.device_mismatch", ip: input.ip, entity: "session", data: { expected: bound, got: device?.deviceId ?? null, tls: tlsVerdict } });
        if (deviceBinding === "enforce") {
          await o.sessions.delete(s.id);
          throw invalid();
        }
      }
      if (device?.fingerprint && s.device?.fingerprint && device.fingerprint !== s.device.fingerprint) {
        await audit({ orgId: s.orgId, userId: s.userId, action: "auth.fingerprint_changed", ip: input.ip, entity: "session", data: { from: s.device.fingerprint, to: device.fingerprint } });
      }
      if (tlsVerdict === "changed") {
        // browser updates and TLS-inspecting middleboxes change it too, so it is logged, never blocking
        await audit({ orgId: s.orgId, userId: s.userId, action: "auth.tls_fingerprint_changed", ip: input.ip, entity: "session", data: { from: s.tlsFingerprintHash, to: tls } });
      }
      if ((device && (device.fingerprint !== s.device?.fingerprint || device.clientSessionId !== s.device?.clientSessionId || input.ip !== s.ip)) || (tls && tls !== s.tlsFingerprintHash)) {
        // keep the device id from login; record the latest fingerprint, tab, info, address and TLS fingerprint
        session = { ...s, lastSeenAt: now, ip: input.ip ?? s.ip, userAgent: input.userAgent ?? s.userAgent, device: device ? { ...s.device, ...device, deviceId: bound ?? device.deviceId } : s.device, tlsFingerprintHash: tls ?? s.tlsFingerprintHash };
        await o.sessions.create(session, idleMs);
      } else {
        await o.sessions.touch(s.id, now, idleMs);
      }
      const next = randomToken();
      const ttl = Math.max(1, s.expiresAt - now);
      await o.kv!.set(`refresh:${hashToken(next)}`, s.id, ttl);
      await o.kv!.set(`refresh-used:${h}`, `${s.id}|${now}`, ttl);
      const access = accessToken(session);
      return { accessToken: access.token, accessExpiresAt: access.expiresAt, refreshToken: next, refreshExpiresAt: refreshExpiry(session, now), user: publicUser(user) };
    },

    /** JWT mode: the claims of a valid access token, without touching storage (for workers or other services). */
    verifyAccessToken(token: string): AccessClaims | null {
      return jwt && looksLikeJwt(token) ? jwt.verify(token) : null;
    },

    /** Token → viewer, or null (unknown, expired, logged out, disabled). Extends the idle window. */
    authenticate,

    /** Everything a request needs. Pass a null/invalid token for an anonymous context. */
    async context(token: string | null | undefined): Promise<AuthContext> {
      const viewer = await authenticate(token);
      if (!viewer) return { viewer: null, can: () => false, branchesFor: () => [], permissions: () => [] };
      const rm = await rolesFor(viewer.orgId);
      return {
        viewer,
        can: (permission, branchId) => can(viewer.roles, permission, rm, branchId),
        branchesFor: (permission) => branchesFor(viewer.roles, permission, rm),
        permissions: (branchId) => permissionsOf(viewer.roles, rm, branchId),
      };
    },

    /** Throws UNAUTHENTICATED / FORBIDDEN; returns the viewer. */
    async require(token: string | null | undefined, permission?: string, branchId?: string | null): Promise<Viewer> {
      const ctx = await this.context(token);
      if (!ctx.viewer) throw new AuthError("UNAUTHENTICATED", "Sign in required");
      if (permission && !ctx.can(permission, branchId)) throw new AuthError("FORBIDDEN", `Missing permission ${permission}`, { permission });
      return ctx.viewer;
    },

    /** Ends the session of an access token (even expired), a refresh token, or an opaque session token. */
    async logout(token: string): Promise<void> {
      const id = sessionIdOf(token);
      let s = id ? await o.sessions.get(id) : null;
      if (!s && jwt && !looksLikeJwt(token)) {
        const sid = await o.kv!.take(`refresh:${hashToken(token)}`);
        s = sid ? await o.sessions.get(sid) : null;
      }
      if (!s) return;
      await o.sessions.delete(s.id);
      await audit({ orgId: s.orgId, userId: s.userId, action: "auth.logout" });
    },

    /** Logs a user out everywhere (optionally keeping the current session). */
    async logoutAll(userId: string, keepToken?: string): Promise<number> {
      return o.sessions.deleteByUser(userId, (keepToken && sessionIdOf(keepToken)) || undefined);
    },

    /** Active sessions ("devices") of a user. `id` can be passed to revokeSession. */
    async sessionsOf(userId: string): Promise<Omit<Session, "userId" | "orgId">[]> {
      return (await o.sessions.listByUser(userId)).map(({ userId: _u, orgId: _o, ...s }) => s).sort((a, b) => b.lastSeenAt - a.lastSeenAt);
    },

    async revokeSession(userId: string, sessionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const s = await o.sessions.get(sessionId);
      if (!s || s.userId !== userId) return false;
      await o.sessions.delete(sessionId);
      return true;
    },

    /** Needs the current password; logs out every other session. */
    async changePassword(input: { userId: string; currentPassword: string; newPassword: string; currentToken?: string }): Promise<void> {
      const user = await o.users.get(input.userId);
      if (!user || !(await verifyPassword(input.currentPassword, user.passwordHash))) throw new AuthError("INVALID_CREDENTIALS", "Current password is incorrect");
      if (input.currentPassword === input.newPassword) throw new AuthError("WEAK_PASSWORD", "Choose a different password");
      await setNewPassword(user, input.newPassword, (input.currentToken && sessionIdOf(input.currentToken)) || undefined);
      await audit({ orgId: user.orgId, userId: user.id, action: "auth.password_change" });
    },

    /**
     * Starts a reset. Returns the token to deliver (email / SMS link), or null when there is no such
     * active user. Respond the same way in both cases, so the endpoint does not reveal accounts.
     */
    async requestPasswordReset(input: { email: string; orgCode?: string; ip?: string }): Promise<{ token: string; expiresAt: Date; user: PublicUser } | null> {
      if (!o.kv) throw new Error("createAuth: pass `kv` to enable password reset");
      const email = normalizeEmail(input.email);
      await limit([input.ip && `reset:ip:${input.ip}`, `reset:email:${email}`]);
      const candidates = (await findCandidates(email, input.orgCode)).filter((u) => u.status === "active");
      if (candidates.length !== 1) return null;
      const user = candidates[0]!;
      const token = randomToken();
      await o.kv.set(`reset:${hashToken(token)}`, user.id, resetTtlMs);
      await audit({ orgId: user.orgId, userId: user.id, action: "auth.reset_requested", ip: input.ip });
      return { token, expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + resetTtlMs), user: publicUser(user) };
    },

    /** Completes a reset: single-use token, new password, every session logged out. */
    async resetPassword(input: { token: string; newPassword: string }): Promise<PublicUser> {
      if (!o.kv) throw new Error("createAuth: pass `kv` to enable password reset");
      const userId = await o.kv.take(`reset:${hashToken(input.token)}`);
      const user = userId ? await o.users.get(userId) : null;
      if (!user || user.status !== "active") throw new AuthError("INVALID_TOKEN", "This reset link is invalid or has expired");
      await setNewPassword(user, input.newPassword);
      await audit({ orgId: user.orgId, userId: user.id, action: "auth.password_reset" });
      return publicUser(user);
    },

    /** Admin sets a password (e.g. new staff). Logs the user out everywhere. */
    async setPassword(userId: string, newPassword: string, actorId?: string): Promise<void> {
      const user = await o.users.get(userId);
      if (!user) throw new AuthError("INVALID_TOKEN", "No such user");
      await setNewPassword(user, newPassword);
      await audit({ orgId: user.orgId, userId: actorId ?? null, action: "auth.password_set", entity: "user", entityId: userId });
    },

    /** Call after editing an organisation's roles, so permission changes apply at once. */
    invalidateRoles(orgId?: string): void {
      if (orgId) roleCache.delete(orgId);
      else roleCache.clear();
    },

    /** For creating users: hash + policy check. */
    async hashNewPassword(password: string, user: { email?: string; name?: string } = {}): Promise<string> {
      assertPasswordPolicy(password, user, o.passwordPolicy);
      return hashPassword(password);
    },
  };
}
```

## File: src/errors.ts

```ts
export type AuthErrorCode =
  | "INVALID_CREDENTIALS"
  | "ACCOUNT_DISABLED"
  | "INVITE_PENDING"
  | "ORG_REQUIRED"
  | "RATE_LIMITED"
  | "WEAK_PASSWORD"
  | "INVALID_TOKEN"
  | "UNAUTHENTICATED"
  | "FORBIDDEN";

const STATUS: Record<AuthErrorCode, number> = {
  INVALID_CREDENTIALS: 401,
  ACCOUNT_DISABLED: 403,
  INVITE_PENDING: 403,
  ORG_REQUIRED: 400,
  RATE_LIMITED: 429,
  WEAK_PASSWORD: 400,
  INVALID_TOKEN: 400,
  UNAUTHENTICATED: 401,
  FORBIDDEN: 403,
};

/** Every auth failure. `code` is stable for clients; `statusCode` suits HTTP and GraphQL extensions. */
export class AuthError extends Error {
  readonly statusCode: number;
  constructor(
    readonly code: AuthErrorCode,
    message: string,
    readonly details: { retryAfterMs?: number; permission?: string } = {},
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "AuthError";
    this.statusCode = STATUS[code];
  }
}
```

## File: src/index.ts

```ts
export { cleanDeviceSignals, createAuth, hashTlsFingerprint, type Auth, type AuthContext, type AuthOptions, type LoginInput, type LoginResult, type PublicUser, type TokenPair, type Viewer } from "./auth";
export { jwtSigner, looksLikeJwt, type AccessClaims, type JwtOptions } from "./jwt";
export { AuthError, type AuthErrorCode } from "./errors";
export { assertPasswordPolicy, hashPassword, hashToken, needsRehash, randomToken, SCRYPT, verifyPassword, type PasswordPolicy } from "./password";
export {
  branchesFor, can, permissionMatches, permissionsOf, PERMISSIONS, roleMap, SYSTEM_ROLES,
  type Permission, type RoleAssignment, type RoleDefinition, type RoleMap,
} from "./rbac";
export { memoryKeyValueStore, memoryRateLimiter, memorySessionStore } from "./memory";
export type { AuditSink, AuthUser, DeviceSignals, KeyValueStore, OrgStore, RateLimiter, RoleStore, Session, SessionStore, UserStatus, UserStore } from "./stores";

## File: src/jwt.ts

```ts
import { createHash, createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

/**
 * Minimal HS256 JSON Web Tokens (RFC 7519) on node:crypto: no dependency. Used for access tokens.
 * Several secrets can be active: the first signs, every one verifies (rotate by prepending a new one,
 * then drop the old one after the access-token lifetime).
 */
export interface JwtOptions {
  /** One secret or a rotation list (first signs). Each at least 32 characters. */
  secret: string | string[];
  issuer?: string;
  audience?: string;
}

export interface AccessClaims {
  /** user id */
  sub: string;
  /** organisation id */
  org: string;
  /** session id (revocable server-side) */
  sid: string;
  iat: number;
  exp: number;
  iss?: string;
  aud?: string;
}

const b64 = (v: string | Buffer) => Buffer.from(v).toString("base64url");
const kidOf = (secret: string) => createHash("sha256").update(secret).digest("base64url").slice(0, 8);

export function jwtSigner(o: JwtOptions) {
  const secrets = (Array.isArray(o.secret) ? o.secret : [o.secret]).filter(Boolean);
  if (!secrets.length) throw new Error("jwt: give at least one secret");
  for (const s of secrets) if (s.length < 32) throw new Error("jwt: every secret needs at least 32 characters");
  const keys = new Map(secrets.map((s) => [kidOf(s), s]));
  const signer = secrets[0]!;
  const mac = (secret: string, data: string) => createHmac("sha256", secret).update(data).digest();

  return {
    sign(claims: Omit<AccessClaims, "iss" | "aud">): string {
      const header = b64(JSON.stringify({ alg: "HS256", typ: "JWT", kid: kidOf(signer) }));
      const body = b64(JSON.stringify({ ...claims, ...(o.issuer ? { iss: o.issuer } : {}), ...(o.audience ? { aud: o.audience } : {}) }));
      return `${header}.${body}.${b64(mac(signer, `${header}.${body}`))}`;
    },

    /** Claims when the signature, issuer and audience hold; null otherwise. `ignoreExpiry` is for logout. */
    verify(token: string, opts: { now?: number; ignoreExpiry?: boolean } = {}): AccessClaims | null {
      if (token.length > 2048) return null;
      const parts = token.split(".");
      if (parts.length !== 3) return null;
      const [h, p, s] = parts as [string, string, string];
      let header: { alg?: string; kid?: string };
      let claims: AccessClaims;
      try {
        header = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(h, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
        claims = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(p, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
      if (header.alg !== "HS256") return null; // never "none", never an algorithm chosen by the token
      const candidates = header.kid && keys.has(header.kid) ? [keys.get(header.kid)!] : secrets;
      const sig = Buffer.from(s, "base64url");
      const ok = candidates.some((secret) => {
        const expected = mac(secret, `${h}.${p}`);
        return expected.length === sig.length && timingSafeEqual(expected, sig);
      });
      if (!ok) return null;
      if (typeof claims.sub !== "string" || typeof claims.org !== "string" || typeof claims.sid !== "string" || typeof claims.exp !== "number") return null;
      if (o.issuer && claims.iss !== o.issuer) return null;
      if (o.audience && claims.aud !== o.audience) return null;
      const now = Math.floor((opts.now ?? Date.now()) / 1000);
      if (!opts.ignoreExpiry && claims.exp <= now) return null;
      return claims;
    },
  };
}

/** A JWT has three dot-separated parts; opaque tokens (base64url) have none. */
export const looksLikeJwt = (token: string) => token.split(".").length === 3;
```

## File: src/memory.ts

```ts
import type { KeyValueStore, RateLimiter, Session, SessionStore } from "./stores";

/**
 * In-process stores: for tests, scripts and single-server development. Production with more than
 * one server needs shared state: use the Redis stores ("@mgpl-diagnostics/auth-kit/redis").
 */

export function memorySessionStore(): SessionStore {
  const sessions = new Map<string, { s: Session; idleUntil: number }>();
  const alive = (id: string) => {
    const e = sessions.get(id);
    if (!e) return null;
    if (e.idleUntil <= Date.now() || e.s.expiresAt <= Date.now()) {
      sessions.delete(id);
      return null;
    }
    return e;
  };
  return {
    async create(s, idleMs) {
      sessions.set(s.id, { s: { ...s }, idleUntil: Math.min(s.expiresAt, Date.now() + idleMs) });
    },
    async get(id) {
      const e = alive(id);
      return e ? { ...e.s } : null;
    },
    async touch(id, lastSeenAt, idleMs) {
      const e = alive(id);
      if (e) {
        e.s.lastSeenAt = lastSeenAt;
        e.idleUntil = Math.min(e.s.expiresAt, Date.now() + idleMs);
      }
    },
    async delete(id) {
      sessions.delete(id);
    },
    async listByUser(userId) {
      return [...sessions.keys()].map(alive).filter((e): e is NonNullable<typeof e> => !!e && e.s.userId === userId).map((e) => ({ ...e.s }));
    },
    async deleteByUser(userId, exceptId) {
      let n = 0;
      for (const [id, e] of sessions) if (e.s.userId === userId && id !== exceptId) { sessions.delete(id); n++; }
      return n;
    },
  };
}

export function memoryKeyValueStore(): KeyValueStore {
  const values = new Map<string, { v: string; until: number }>();
  return {
    async set(key, value, ttlMs) {
      values.set(key, { v: value, until: Date.now() + ttlMs });
    },
    async take(key) {
      const e = values.get(key);
      values.delete(key);
      return e && e.until > Date.now() ? e.v : null;
    },
  };
}

/** Sliding window: at most `limit` hits per `windowMs` per key. */
export function memoryRateLimiter(o: { limit: number; windowMs: number }): RateLimiter {
  const hits = new Map<string, number[]>();
  return {
    async hit(key) {
      const now = Date.now();
      const list = (hits.get(key) ?? []).filter((t) => t > now - o.windowMs);
      if (list.length >= o.limit) {
        hits.set(key, list);
        return { allowed: false, retryAfterMs: list[0]! + o.windowMs - now };
      }
      list.push(now);
      hits.set(key, list);
      return { allowed: true, retryAfterMs: 0 };
    },
    async reset(key) {
      hits.delete(key);
    },
    async undo(key) {
      hits.get(key)?.pop();
    },
  };
}
```
